mt: 'INTERNATIONAL INSTITUTE OF SOCIAL HISTORY' IN AI MODE — THE INSTITUTE AT ITS GRAIN; THE PAPERS OF MARX, ENGELS AND BAKUNIN NAMED IN ONE CUSTODY
d: THE INSTITUTE, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-31, AI MODE: 'The International Institute of Social History (IISH; Dutch: Internationaal Instituut voor Sociale Geschiedenis, IISG) is one of the world's premier archives and research centers dedicated to global labor and social history.' Fact table (founded 25 November 1935, Posthumus, KNAW); core pillars: the archive, radical papers, rescue of endangered heritage, the data hub.
reading: The innocent reading first. Asked for the institute, AI Mode gives its founding, affiliation, holdings, rescues and data, and offers to help plan a visit.
findings: ONE CUSTODY FOR BOTH SIDES OF THE HAGUE. 'Its vaults contain the irreplaceable personal papers and manuscripts of major historical figures like Karl Marx, Friedrich Engels, Mikhail Bakunin, Emma Goldman, and Leon Trotsky.' The parties to the First International's 1872 expulsion (#1725, line 67) are held by one institution, for the papers it holds; the archive's own deposits place the 1844 manuscripts in the Russian State Archive of Socio-Political History (RGASPI) in Moscow, 'where the manuscripts are currently held' (#843).

THE RESCUE CARRIED. 'Originally founded to rescue endangered heritage from totalitarian regimes (such as Nazi Germany and Franco's Spain)'. The census's two saved pages state its founding year ('The IISH was officially established in 1935') and do not carry the rescue; its Wikipedia card does, and the composition cites it to the International Consortium of Critical Theory.
analysis: A faithful account of the institute, with the feature the census asks of an archive of the left: the papers of the winning and losing sides of a split in one custody, for the papers it holds.
